name: VerusBridge duplicate-proof-root parser divergence
summary: The bridge's NotarizationSerializer took the last proof-root entry when a notarization listed the same system ID twice, while Verus consensus used the first. Notary-signed notarizations with duplicate entries let the attacker install and confirm its own Verus state root on Ethereum, then prove an unbacked import against it and drain the bridge's reserves.
notes: Reset: upgrade 0xb29f45f3 routed the Delegator's notarization path to NotarizationSerializer 0x95b8005c in the July 2026 redeploy; no later write to that route. The May 2026 exploit hit the earlier import code and is a separate incident.

Anchor: the attacker's first notarization already carried duplicate VRSC proof-root entries (six system-ID occurrences against four in honest ones) and installed its root; the second confirmed it and 0xa1f1e65c consumed it to pay out.
Loss: bridge-held ETH and tokens plus DAI drawn from the bridge's DSR position; DefiLlama prices for ETH, tBTC, MKR and scrvUSD, par for the stablecoins.
